title: Reduce nondeterministic prefill races with per-stream epoch fencing and assertive kernel probing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see intermittent downstream correctness failures and token duplication in high-concurrency decode workloads that use CUDA Graph-based capture/replay. Investigation indicates nondeterministic interleaving between prefill windows on adjacent streams and speculative kernel binding decisions that assume a consistent KV state. This ticket introduces a per-stream epoch-fencing mechanism and assertive kernel-probing step during capture to ensure a deterministic capture snapshot and safe replay conditions.

Goal: Eliminate race-induced replay correctness failures under high-concurrency, preemptible GPU conditions while keeping end-to-end latency regression <5% p50 and throughput degradation <8% under typical RLHF-like traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: No reproduced token duplication or out-of-order outputs in the stress harness (5M requests across 48-hour run) at 95th percentile concurrency
End-to-end median latency regression <5% on internal benchmark suite compared to baseline runtime-1.20
Automated correctness asserts detect any epoch-mismatch during capture and surface an actionable error in tracing logs
Feature gated rollout works for canary fleet and allows instant fallback to current capture mode with zero client-visible errors
design_notes: Per-stream epoch fencing: assign monotonically increasing epoch id to a stream when entering prefill mode. Any capture must record stream_epoch; replay will validate stream_epoch against active epoch to avoid stale-snapshot replay.

Assertive kernel probing: before committing a CUDA Graph capture, run a fast, idempotent kernel-probe that exercises the same attention kernel path to validate kernel selection and occupancy assumptions for the current sequence length and quantization mode.
KV snapshot tagging: include a lightweight KV epoch hash in capture metadata. If KV hash mismatches at replay, trigger safe fallback path instead of attempting replay.
Quiesce window hysteresis: add a small, adaptive quiesce delay when stream contention exceeds threshold to reduce capture collisions; tuned by observed arrival inter-arrival distribution.
Fallback semantics: if validation fails, opt for non-cached decode on that stream for the request, log and emit metric; do not block other streams.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Extra kernel-probe adds a small compute overhead before capture which could slightly increase tail latency for cold requests; mitigated by quick probe kernels and batching probes across closely-scheduled captures.

Epoch fencing requires careful lifecycle management to avoid epoch churn during autoscaling events; need to integrate with the existing stream allocator to persist epoch across brief preemption recoveries.
There is a risk of false positives if KV hash computation is too strict (e.g., includes non-deterministic metadata); choose canonicalized KV fingerprinting to avoid spurious fallbacks.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike - 3d): implement epoch id on StreamContext and add trace points. Prototype kernel-probe harness and KV fingerprint function. Run small smoke tests.
Phase 2 (dev - 5d): integrate assertive probe into capture commit path behind feature flag. Emit new metrics: capture_probe_latency, epoch_mismatch_count, probe_failure_count.
Phase 3 (qa - 4d): run long-running stress harness with mixed sequence lengths, quant modes, and preemption churn. Validate correctness and measure perf.
Phase 4 (canary - 7d): rollout to 10% canary machines + dedicated fleet under traffic profile A. Monitor metrics and errors, iterate on hysteresis tuning.
Phase 5 (gradual rollout - 5d): increase to 50% then 100% with rollback window and runbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for epoch assignment and KV fingerprinting logic
Determinism harness: reproduce previously flaky scenario (see reproducer/epoch_fence_v2.py) and assert no mismatch
End-to-end long-run stress test in CI: 48 hours, multi-tenant QPS profile, verify no correctness regressions
Chaos test: simulate preemption and stream reallocation while capturing and replaying to validate epoch resilience
rollout_plan: Gate the feature behind runtime-config flag 'epoch_fence_v1' and a per-cluster sampler.
Start canary on non-critical clusters (10% machines) with synthetic workloads. Monitor errors for 48h.
If metrics stable, expand to dedicated inference fleet used by internal customers, then public canaries.
Provide immediate rollback by disabling feature flag which reverts capture commit to previous code path; include runbook steps for support on-call.
dependencies_notes: Needs StreamAllocator API extension (ENG-206543) to persist epoch across brief stream handoffs.
Relies on a small KV fingerprint util (can share with caching infra) to avoid duplication of hashing code.
Coordination with telemetry team to add new metrics and tracing spans.
